svg.title: LatentLab: a bigger importance sample is not a realization-wise guarantee
svg.desc: Twelve neural importance-prefix rows distinguish log mean weight from mean log weight. An exact linear-Gaussian control recovers the evidence with its true posterior. A rare-atom control has ESS 64 while underestimating evidence almost one million-fold on an event with probability 93.80 percent.
svg.text: A larger sample is not a realization-wise guarantee
Neural VAE anchor x = (1,0) | shared Gaussian-noise prefixes, seed 107 | natural log density units
log mean w: a random log-evidence estimate. mean log w: sampled ELBO integrand, not analytic-KL MC.
Within each row: log mean w >= mean log w. Across K: realized log mean w can go up or down.
ESS: 64.00 / 64 | constant weights for any proposal-noise draws
This separate control has an analytic answer; the nonlinear VAE does not.
Proposal: (0.999, 0.001). Full support, but poorly matched.
ESS = 64, log estimate = -13.814510; true log evidence = 0
Expected log estimate: finite binomial enumeration, not one random realization
Exact rational mean evidence estimate = 1 at every K. Expected log estimates stay below 0 and rise with K.
High ESS only describes weight balance in the observed cloud. It cannot detect the missed rare atom.
No IWAE training is implemented. Gaussian-reference evidence is exact; neural evidence remains unknown.
Expectation bounds require valid IID full-support proposals. Supplied noise values alone do not prove those assumptions.
Standard importance/IWAE formulas credited to Burda, Grosse & Salakhutdinov. Original finite audit and fixtures.
